html:
SMTO-EXE-0239 — This Docker action needs your approval first

GUID: 4392a156-3d5c-5ca0-938c-8447f8bca93a
Slug: docker-privileged-operation-requires-confirmation
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Docker action you asked for can affect the Gateway computer itself, for example by giving a container access to its files or network. SMTO won't do this without someone approving it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look in the task for the approval request, read what access it asks for, then select Approve once if you agree, or Deny / stop task if not. SMTO needs a person to agree before a container can reach the Gateway computer's files, network or devices.
  2. If no approval request appears and the action is refused, open Settings › Security › Policy / Permissions and see whether it is set to Deny. A Deny setting blocks these actions without asking anyone.
  3. Ask the person who manages SMTO before changing that setting, or ask SMTO to do the job without the extra access, for example without mounting host folders. Removing the extra access is often enough and avoids needing approval at all.

What success looks like

  • After you approve, the Docker action runs and the task shows its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with what you asked the container to do. Don't set Permissions to Allow just to get past this; SMTO would then stop asking before other risky actions too.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A host-affecting Docker operation (privileged mode, host network/PID/IPC, devices, added capabilities, host bind mounts, Docker socket mounts, code execution or Compose changes) needs authorization through the shared unsafe-action approval flow; this diagnostic itself grants nothing.

What this means

  • A host-affecting-operation confirmation identity is retained, but current Docker authorization is owned by the shared unsafe-action policy rather than a direct producer of this category. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A host-affecting-operation confirmation identity is retained, but current Docker authorization is owned by the shared unsafe-action policy rather than a direct producer of this category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current operation risks and the owning run's unsafe-action decision, not this compatibility label alone.

How to fix it

  • Route the exact operation through the existing unsafe-action approval (Approve once on the approval card, or Allow with a wider scope selected there) and check the effective rule in Settings › Security › Policy / Permissions or the conversation/prompt override. Do not treat this error as permission; confirm the request's risks list (privileged, host_bind, docker_socket, etc.) is intended.
  • Use the existing unsafe-action flow for the exact host-affecting operation; do not infer permission from this diagnostic.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual shared policy authorizes the exact intended action and its current prerequisites hold.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
